sources.title: ONS UK Environmental Accounts: 2026
facts: ONS environmental accounts use a residence-basis framework that differs from territorial inventories.
The 2026 bulletin links atmospheric-emissions and energy-use evidence through 2024.
National environmental-account statistics do not establish individual parcel emissions.

sources.title: ONS Environment, climate and nature insights, UK: 2026
facts: ONS issued corrections on 24 July 2026 and removed unreliable climate-related mortality estimates pending an updated release.
Corrections and superseded values must be preserved in provenance rather than silently merged.
Environmental insight indicators are not individual parcel greenhouse-gas measurements.

sources.title: ONS Atmospheric emissions: greenhouse gases by industry and gas
facts: The dataset covers greenhouse-gas emissions by industry and gas for 1990 to 2024.
Current and provisional editions have different completeness and revision status.
Industry-level emissions are not parcel-bound observations.

sources.title: ONS Atmospheric emissions: greenhouse gases by industry and gas — current
facts: The current edition provides data for all economic sectors.
Scheduled revisions and correction history are explicitly documented.
Current-edition status does not remove the need to preserve accounting basis and reference period.

sources.title: ONS Atmospheric emissions: greenhouse gases by industry and gas — provisional
facts: The provisional edition provides top-level estimates and remains revision-sensitive.
ONS documents a March 2026 correction to some 2023 carbon-dioxide values in an earlier provisional file.
Provisional statistics must not be represented as final parcel measurements.

sources.title: ONS Atmospheric emissions bridging tables
facts: Bridging tables relate environmental-account measures to UNFCCC and UNECE measures for 1990 to 2024.
Bridging relationships highlight differences between accounting frameworks.
A bridge table is methodology evidence rather than parcel-level measurement evidence.

sources.title: ONS Energy use: total
facts: The dataset covers direct and reallocated UK energy use by industry through 2024.
Energy use and greenhouse-gas emissions are distinct measures.
No parcel emissions value may be inferred without parcel activity and a verified conversion method.

sources.title: ONS Energy use: renewable and waste sources
facts: The dataset covers renewable and waste energy use by source and industry through 2024.
Renewable-energy activity is not equivalent to measured emissions reduction.
Industry-level activity must not be silently assigned to individual parcels.

sources.title: ONS Energy use: by industry, source and fuel
facts: Energy use is disaggregated by industry, source and fuel.
Fuel and source classifications must be preserved when comparing or converting data.
Activity data require an explicit emissions-factor method before any emissions estimate.

sources.title: DfT Statistics at DfT
facts: The DfT statistics page lists SAF and RTFO fifth provisional releases dated 23 July 2026.
Vehicle licensing January to March 2026 was published 15 July 2026 and transport-environment statistics on 14 July 2026.
Publication chronology must be preserved to avoid treating future or superseded releases as current observations.

sources.title: DfT Transport and environment statistics: 2024
facts: The release reports environmental impacts of transport including greenhouse gases and air pollutants for the UK.
The release reports 110.4 MtCO2e for domestic transport in 2024.
National transport totals cannot be assigned to individual parcels.

sources.title: DfT Transport energy and environment data tables
facts: ENV tables contain fuel-consumption and emissions measures with differing periods of coverage.
Each table's reference period and source definitions must be preserved.
Transport-mode statistics are not direct parcel emissions measurements.

sources.title: DfT Transport energy and environment statistics collection
facts: The collection identifies Transport and environment statistics: 2024 as the latest official release.
Collection tables draw on multiple accredited official-statistics sources.
Collection-level metadata must not override the definitions of underlying datasets.

sources.title: Ofgem BUS monthly scheme update
facts: The July update covers scheme activity through 30 June 2026.
Voucher applications, vouchers and grants are scheme-administration measures.
BUS uptake is not a measured greenhouse-gas reduction for an individual parcel.

sources.title: Ofgem Boiler Upgrade Scheme guidance for installers
facts: Version 5.1 is the current installer guidance for relevant applications.
Updated uplifted grant guidance applies to eligible off-gas-grid applications from 21 July 2026.
Eligibility and grant guidance are policy and administration evidence, not emissions observations.

sources.title: Ofgem Boiler Upgrade Scheme
facts: BUS provides grants for eligible low-carbon heating technologies in England and Wales.
Current grant categories include an uplift for eligible off-gas-grid heat-pump installations from 21 July 2026.
Grant value cannot be converted into parcel emissions savings without a separate verified method.

sources.title: Ofgem Boiler Upgrade Scheme Product Eligibility List
facts: The Product Eligibility List was updated 23 July 2026.
A listed product can still be ineligible for BUS for another reason.
Product eligibility does not establish measured greenhouse-gas performance at parcel level.

sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS
facts: UK ETS operators submit verified emissions reports and surrender allowances under defined scheme rules.
Domestic maritime emissions entered UK ETS scope from 1 July 2026 for qualifying activity.
Compliance and allowance data are not equivalent to parcel-level physical emissions measurements.

sources.title: UK ETS policy overview
facts: The policy overview describes maritime expansion from July 2026 and waste-sector expansion policy.
Policy scope, MRV requirements and future scheme expansion must be separated from observed emissions.
Policy targets and compliance architecture do not create parcel measurements.

sources.title: Voluntary MRV period for waste incineration
facts: A voluntary MRV-only period for EfW and waste-incineration facilities began 1 January 2026.
The guidance prepares facilities for future UK ETS expansion.
Participation or facility scope does not itself establish a parcel-level greenhouse-gas value.
